steps.text: The rate is increasing linearly, and its value at the middle of the interval is its average over the interval.

stem:
A farmer has 120 m of fencing for three sides of a rectangular enclosure beside a straight river. The fourth side needs no fence. Let each perpendicular side have length $x$ metres.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: c

steps.text: Dimensions 30 m by 60 m; area $1800$ square metres.
The derivative changes from positive to negative at 30, so this is a maximum.
The total enclosed three-side length becomes 124, so $A=x(124-2x)$.

title: Minimizing material for an open cylindrical container
stem:
An open cylindrical container must hold 500 cubic centimetres. Its radius is $r$ cm and its height is $h$ cm. The base and curved side use the same material; there is no lid.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the surface area can be written $S(r)=\pi r^2+1000/r$, for $r>0$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the radius and height minimizing surface area.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain the relationship between optimal height and radius and find the minimum area.

steps.text: Use $h=500/(\pi r^2)$ from the volume constraint.
Substitute into $S=\pi r^2+2\pi rh$ and simplify.
For positive r, multiplying the derivative by positive r squared preserves its sign. Its sign is that of $2\pi r^3-1000$, which changes from negative to positive at this radius.
The stationary equation gives $2\pi r^3=1000$, hence $h=r$.

title: Using a rate graph to compare production levels
stem:
The derivative of cumulative production F is $F\prime(t)=t^2-6t+8$ units per hour, for $0\leq t\leq5$. The derivative graph is shown. The quantity F here represents a net production balance and can decrease.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: b

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A student says F is zero at both 2 and 4 because the graph crosses the axis there. Explain the mistake.

steps.text: At $t=2$ the derivative changes positive to negative, giving a local maximum.
At $t=4$ it changes negative to positive, giving a local minimum.
The plotted graph is of the derivative, not F.
The crossings show zero rates of change, not zero values of the cumulative balance.

answerSummary: Increasing for $0<t<2$ and $4<t<5$; decreasing for $2<t<4$.

steps.text: Add the initial volume; divide entering volume by eight for the average rate.
Final $748/3=249.333\ldots$ cubic metres; average $56/3=18.6667\ldots$ cubic metres per hour.
The rate changes over the interval.
Using the final rate treats all eight hours as though the flow had always been 20 cubic metres per hour.

stem:

steps.text: Divide the absolute difference by the exact area and multiply by 100.

The derivative is the instantaneous marginal cost at exactly 20 units; the finite one-unit change averages the changing marginal cost over $20\leq x\leq21$.

title: A fixed-area garden with unequal fencing costs
stem:
A rectangular garden has area 96 square metres. One pair of opposite sides has fencing costing 18 per metre; the other pair costs 8 per metre. Let $x$ be the length of each expensive side.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: b

steps.text: Expensive sides $6.53197$ m; other sides $14.6969$ m.
The derivative changes from negative to positive, giving a minimum.
A square has side $\sqrt{96}$ and cost $52\sqrt{96}$.
The expensive sides should be shorter, even though this increases the cheaper sides.

steps.text: The tangent estimate is $10.44$; evaluate the actual cubic at 2.2.

title: Optimising an advertisement with a minimum margin
stem:
A rectangular poster has total area 600 square centimetres. The printed region must leave 2 cm margins at the left and right and 3 cm at the top and bottom. Let the poster width be $x$ cm.

Use technology where appropriate. Retain unrounded values until the final answer; give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless money or another precision is specified.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the printed area in terms of $x$ and give a suitable domain.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the poster dimensions that maximize printed area.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the fraction of the poster that is printed and compare the width-to-height ratio with the ratio of total horizontal to total vertical margins.

steps.text: Poster height is $600/x$; printed dimensions are $x-4$ and $600/x-6$.
The derivative is positive before 20 and negative after 20, so this is a maximum.
Printed fraction $384/600=0.64$; poster ratio $20:30=2:3$, equal to the margin ratio $4:6$.
